```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is one paying customer in 90 days, not scale. B's buyers are B2B SaaS teams with a product budget and a validated $25-79/mo entry price, so a single conversion is meaningful revenue. A's quoted demand says caregivers want it 'free to use' because they are 'financially stressed,' and competitors already offer generous free tiers.",
    "B's buyers (indie builders, early-stage SaaS teams) gather in documented low-cash channels like Product Hunt and Indie Hackers. The brief cites a launch that converted 68 signups from 170 visitors. A's own brief concedes that incumbents already win its organic Reddit channel, and its paid channel evidence is weak.",
    "A has structural activation and retention problems that B lacks. It needs multiple siblings to adopt it, and customer lifetime ends when the parent moves to facility care or dies. A single B buyer can adopt and pay alone.",
    "A's regulatory exposure is heavier for a solo operator. The FTC Health Breach Notification Rule may apply, and Washington's My Health My Data Act carries a private right of action. B's GDPR/CCPA DPA and privacy setup is a standard, templatable one-time draft with periodic review.",
    "Both categories are saturated: six or more live competitors in A, a 73-tool pricing study in B. Saturation therefore does not separate them. Payer economics and ease of first conversion do, and both favor B."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's paid-social CAC evidence is a 2017 WordStream general Facebook CPC benchmark (~$1-3). It is roughly a decade old and not specific to caregivers or this category, so it says almost nothing about the real cost of acquiring a paying caregiver. Close behind is the first demand quote, which comes from a founder promoting their own app rather than from a prospective buyer.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe crowded, commoditized markets, and neither shows an unclaimed wedge. B's demand evidence is thin: one quote is from a builder solving their own pain, and the other is a price complaint from an older Reddit thread. B's Product Hunt figures are a single anecdote. B wins mainly on payer economics and a clearer route to a first paid conversion, not on strong demand proof."
}
```
